thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Prod alert: pod crash loop and OOM events detected on prod-serving-3 (us-west-2). 18 failures in last 10m, increasing CUDA driver errors reported. Auto-created incident channel #incident-1715001234.
ashita: I'm on it — grabbing logs from the node and checking recent deploys. Can someone @mike for runtime?
mike: @ashita oncall here. seeing a pattern: paged-attn allocator showing gradual resident growth on KV cache slabs. Not an immediate spike, looks like slow creeping fragmentation.
sarah: any customer-facing errors yet?
trent: some customers reporting 5xxs and latency spikes, notably session-based chat workloads. Support routing a few escalations.
ashita: ok, priority: 1) contain blast radius 2) gather diagnostics 3) mitigation plan. First step: throttle new session acceptance on prod-serving-3 and move traffic. @ops-bot can you cordon and drain one affected node?
ops-bot: executing: `kubectl cordon gpu-prod-3 && kubectl drain gpu-prod-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — started.
mike: dumping allocator stats from the runtime:
```
KV cache slab usage: total=248GB, free_frag=46GB, largest_chunk=2MB
paged-attn pages: resident=182GB, paged_out=66GB
per-alloc growth: +1.2MB/min across ~1200 active contexts
OOM count (last 30m): 12
CUDA errors: 24 (cuCtxSynchronize timeout, out of memory)
```
ashita: that growth rate implies we have a creeping per-request leak, likely in the merge path when attention pages are converted for fused kernels. Any recent merges?
mike: rolled quant_conv optimization 2 days ago, but telemetry didn't flag before. I suspect a corner when page compaction fails and we create new slabs instead of reusing.
sarah: quick mitigation idea: lower max KV cache per-request and bump eviction aggressiveness to force compaction. We can also pin critical customers to other regions.
trent: doing customer triage: highest-impact customers (3 tenants) seeing 10-30% error rates. One is on a Dedicated cluster — pushing them to standby region now.
nashita: let's apply runtime config change on prod-serving fleet to reduce kv_max_bytes_per_ctx from 64MB -> 16MB and set eviction threshold to 60%. Doing a staged rollout (canary 5%). @mike will watch memory metrics.
mike: applying canary to 5% now via rollout tool.
nashita: can we also enable periodic slab compaction immediately? How expensive is that?
mike: compaction is ~5–7% CPU spike for a short window, but it compacts fragments back into larger extents — should recover free_frag quickly. I'll enable it on the canary.
nashita: ops-bot reports drain finished and pod relocated off gpu-prod-3. Node shows several coredumps. I'll upload to the debug bucket.
nashita: attaching core excerpt:
```
#0  0x7f8a3b4d in gcc_kv_allocator::allocate_fragment() at kv_alloc.cc:412
#1  0x7f8a3c11 in paged_attention::page_attach() at paged_attn.cc:289
#2  0x7f8a3ee2 in fused_attention::run() at fused_attn.cu:118
```
mike: that stack aligns with a failed compaction path where we bail and allocate new fragment. If compaction fails repeatedly we keep creating small fragments until OOM.
sarah: timeline note for incident doc: first anomalous metric 1714998000 (slow growth), first OOM 1714999200, escalate alert 1715001200. Root ts is this thread 1715001234.
trent: customer comms drafted: short note, we're investigating memory growth causing API errors, mitigation in progress (traffic rerouted, config changes). ETA for full recovery TBD.
nashita: can someone run `pmap`/`nvidia-smi` dump from the affected host and paste? Need to correlate process RSS with GPU memory.
mike: pasted below:
```
PID 1234 runtime-server  RSS 42GB  GPU 7: 12000MiB
PID 1256 worker-1        RSS 10GB  GPU 7: 11000MiB
```
Looks like single runtime process holding a lot of GPU memory and not freeing.
nashita: for the canary with reduced kv_max_bytes_per_ctx, memory curve is flattening on the canary nodes. Can we promote?
mike: canary looks good for 12m: no new OOMs, CUDA errors reduced. I'll roll to 30% and enable compaction cluster-wide once 30% stable.
sarah: coordinate with oncall rotation — handing over to night oncall after we stabilize. @mike please add short runbook snippet for the next shift: how to detect creeping fragmentation and temporary mitigations (reduce kv size, force compaction, node drain).
mike: done, added to the incident doc. Key commands:
```
# lower kv per-ctx
curl -XPOST https://controlplane/rollouts -d '{"kv_max_bytes_per_ctx": 16777216}'
# force compaction
kubectl exec -c runtime $POD -- /usr/local/bin/runtime ctl compact-slabs --target=aggressive
# quick node drain
kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
ops-bot: rollout to 30% completed. enabling compaction via runtime ctl across cluster.
trent: customers updated: one tenant moved to standby, two are seeing degraded throughput but fewer errors. Support queue has 12 open tickets tied to this.
nashita: monitoring for the next 2 hours. If fragmentation resumes, we'll consider reverting the quant_conv optimization and a fleet-wide restart.
mike: creating a follow-up task for an allocator patch to ensure compaction fallback doesn't leak fragments. Assigning to @mike and @sarah.
sarah: acknowledged. Also adding perf eval to the PR so we ensure we don't reintroduce regressions.
nashita: handing off to night oncall @mike (oncall). Incident severity currently P2 (elevated customer impact but mitigated). Please update incident channel and incident tracker.
trent: I'll send a post-incident customer follow-up once root cause confirmed.
nashita: thanks team. Closing in-channel ops; keeping incident open until allocator patch and verification complete. :white_check_mark:
